title: Annotatio III §.VI: Berengar revokes the forced palinode — Hildebrand/Gregory VII beats him into a new substantial-conversion formula
pass_a_gloss: Nay at length, when Berengar, ill at ease with himself for having denied the truth, had returned to himself and by a published writing revoked his own revocation as no less absurd than impious, and had signified that it had been extorted from him by force by a Council of the malignant Church and of vanity, he was summoned by Hildebrand (by others Hellenbrand), called Gregory VII, to a Roman Council and beaten with rods to a new recantation; three months’ truce being granted, he was afterward compelled, a palinode or profession of this sort being thrust upon him, by which under the Pope’s most grave precept it was thereafter to be confessed that the mystic bread is substantially converted into the true and proper flesh of Christ.
pass_b_english: Berengar, conscience-struck, published a revocation of that forced palinode as absurd and impious, calling the council a church of the malignant and of vanity.
Hildebrand (Gregory VII) summoned him to Rome, beat him with rods, and after a three-month truce forced a new formula: mystic bread substantially converted into Christ’s true proper flesh.
source_text: Quin tandem, cum Berengarius, ob negatam veritatem, sibi malè conscius, ad seipsum rediisset, & suam ipsius revocationem non minus absurdam quam impiam, scripto editô revocasset, eamque per vim sibi extortam esse ab Ecclesia malignantium & vanitatis Concilio, significasset, ab Hildebrando, aliis Hellenbrando, Gregorio VII. appellato, ad Romanum Concilium evocatus virgisque cæsus ad novam recantationem, trium mensium concessis induciis, coactus postliminio est, obtrusâ palinodiæ seu professionis ejusmodi formulâ, quâ panem mysticum substantialiter converti in veram & propriam carnem Christi, sub gravissimo Papæ præcepto, deinceps confitendum erat.
